title: Elodie and the Portrait
premise: Ivo Voss, a meticulous pest controller who trusts counts and seals over feelings, is called to the Harrow estate after workers report something leaving fingerprints on the inside of a door they unearthed — a door sealed from within. As night falls, Ivo and the excavation crew realize the house has been waiting for someone to open what was never meant to be opened, and that the invitation was written generations ago in the Voss family's own hand. To survive until sunrise, Ivo must confront his inherited duty as the last of the line invited to keep the thing fed, choosing between the love he's found with site surveyor Mara Kell and the obligation stitched into his blood. He ends the inheritance by burning the ledger of names at dawn, sealing himself out of the family bargain forever — but not without leaving something of himself behind on the other side of the door.
about_author: Noor Eriksen is a former building conservator who spent years cataloguing sealed rooms in Nordic manor houses before turning to horror. She writes in a converted boathouse on the Oslofjord, where she claims every door is counted twice.

chapters.title: Fingerprints
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Called to the Harrow estate after a foreman finds small fingerprints on the inside face of an unearthed cellar door, Ivo inspects, dusts, and counts — and finds prints matching no living worker, pressed from within. The beat: professional calm cracking into unease as his methodical world fails to explain the evidence.

chapters.title: The Counting Man
chapters.summary: POV Ivo, flashback-tinged. We learn Ivo's rituals: lights kept on, doors counted nightly, a habit inherited from a father who never explained it. A phone call from his estranged aunt warns him not to take jobs 'with old doors.' The beat: dread rooted in childhood, establishing inheritance as wound.

chapters.title: Mara Draws the Lines
chapters.summary: POV Mara Kell, site surveyor. Mapping the excavation, she notes the door sits precisely on no recorded foundation — older than the house above it. She and Ivo share coffee and cautious flirtation; she shows him her sketch of the doorframe carvings. The beat: warmth and connection, the love that duty will threaten.

chapters.title: Sealed From Inside
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Examination confirms the impossible: bolts thrown, wax poured, all from the room's interior. Something locked itself in — or was locked in by agreement. That evening the crew's generator dies though its fuel is full. The beat: the rational explanation collapses; the house begins asserting itself.

chapters.title: The Crew That Wouldn't Leave
chapters.summary: POV crew chief Denny Okafor. Denny tries to pull his team off the job, but three men refuse — one keeps returning to the pit, murmuring that he's been 'expected.' Denny stays to fetch them back. The beat: compulsion takes hold; the trap closes around people who should have walked away.

chapters.title: What Was Invited In
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. In the estate archive Ivo finds a ledger bearing his surname: the Voss family, for six generations, listed as 'keepers' who renewed an invitation every fifty years. The last renewal date is overdue — this year. The beat: horror becomes personal; the fingerprints are addressed to him.

chapters.title: Nightfall Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Sunset comes early behind storm clouds. Mara counts heads — nine souls on site — and watches the number feel wrong, like the house is holding a place open for a tenth. She and Ivo admit what they mean to each other, quietly, as if rationing it. The beat: tenderness sharpened by countdown.

chapters.title: The Tenth Place
chapters.summary: POV Denny. At dinner the table sets itself for ten. The missing worker, Pell, is found standing at the pit edge, answering questions no one asked. When Denny grabs him, Pell's voice comes out layered, patient, ancient. The beat: first direct contact; the entity speaks through the taken.

chapters.title: Doors Within Doors
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Every door in the estate now shows fresh fingerprints on their inner faces. Ivo realizes the cellar door was never the boundary — it was the mouth. His counting ritual, meant to protect, has been teaching the house his habits. The beat: his armor turned against him.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Ivo, reading aloud. The ledger's terms surface: each keeper feeds the thing one name per generation, or it takes freely. His father's final entry is blank — he died before paying. Ivo understands why his father counted doors: he was stalling. The beat: grief reframed; the inheritance revealed as debt.

chapters.title: Pell Comes Home
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Pell returns at midnight, smiling, wrong, leading two others toward the pit like children following a teacher. Mara bars the doorway with her body and her survey stakes, buying minutes with iron and nerve. The beat: courage under pressure; love made physical in defense.

chapters.title: What the Lights Are For
chapters.summary: POV Denny. The lights fail floor by floor, exactly in the order Ivo checks them. Denny realizes the house learned the route from Ivo's rituals and is walking it backward toward them. They regroup in the archive, the only room whose door still holds. The beat: siege logic; safety shrinking to a single room.

chapters.title: A Name in the Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. The entity offers terms through Pell's mouth: write any name, any name at all, and the rest go free. It suggests Mara's. Ivo nearly writes it — pen touching paper — then sees his own reflection in the inkwell wearing his father's face. The beat: temptation at its cruelest; the cost of love weaponized.

chapters.title: Mara's Excavation
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Refusing to be saved or sacrificed, Mara digs into the survey records and finds the truth: the door predates the Voss family. They weren't born keepers — they volunteered, generations ago, to contain something they themselves disturbed. The beat: agency reclaimed; the myth of duty exposed as choice.

chapters.title: The Room Behind the Door
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Through a hairline crack, Ivo sees inside: not a monster but a crowded dark full of every paid name, standing patiently, waiting to be remembered. Among them, unmistakably, his father. The beat: horror transfigured into heartbreak; the enemy revealed as the accumulated dead.

chapters.title: Sunrise Terms
chapters.summary: POV Denny. Dawn is forty minutes out and the entity grows desperate, dropping pretense, shaking the estate to its studs. Denny holds the stairwell alone so Ivo can reach the ledger, taking wounds that don't bleed right. The beat: sacrifice; friendship proven in blood and splinters.

chapters.title: The Burning Page
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. At the ledger, Ivo refuses both options — payment and refusal — and instead burns the book page by page, unmaking the contract itself. The house screams through every door at once. His father's voice, briefly clear, says only: 'Count nothing. Go.' The beat: climax; inheritance ended by fire.

chapters.title: Sealed From Outside
chapters.summary: POV Mara. With the pact broken, the doors swing wide and the cold pours out — but the thing, uninvited now, cannot cross thresholds it was never asked through. Mara drags the wounded out into grey dawn light while Ivo nails the cellar door shut from the outside, mirroring the original seal. The beat: reversal complete; the hunters become the sealed.

chapters.title: Headcount
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. In the daylight, Ivo counts the living: eight. Pell is gone — taken into the dark when the contract burned, a price with no receipt. Ivo performs his ritual one last time, then deliberately stops mid-count, hands shaking. The beat: mourning braided with liberation.

chapters.title: What Ivo Left Behind
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Weeks later, Mara notices Ivo's shadow lags a half-second, and that mirrors show him a shade too pale. Part of him stayed on the other side of the door — the part that was Voss. She chooses to stay anyway. The beat: bittersweet resolution; love accepting damage rather than abandoning it.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Ivo writes a new book — not a ledger of debts but a record of names to remember: his father's, Pell's, all the paid ones recovered from Mara's archives. Keeping memory, he decides, is a duty worth choosing. The beat: transformation of inheritance into remembrance.

chapters.title: Elodie
chapters.summary: POV Mara, coda. Mara finally asks about the name carved faintly inside the unearthed door: Elodie, the first Voss volunteer, the one who sealed it from within to buy her family time. Ivo plants flowers over the filled pit. Somewhere below, something patient begins, very slowly, to count. The beat: quiet dread restored; the story ends where it began, listening.
